conbody.p: HBO_MAX_READ_TIME_MS query option The HBO_MAX_READ_TIME_MS query option limits the total time that the planner spends reading History Based Optimization (HBO) statistics for one query.

When USE_HBO_STATS is enabled, the planner looks up historical cardinality statistics for each supported plan node. If the HBO cache backend is slow, these lookups can add noticeable time to query planning. An example is a remote Redis or Valkey server that is configured with the --hbo_cache_backend=redis startup flag. Set HBO_MAX_READ_TIME_MS to bound that time. Once the limit is reached, the planner stops reading HBO statistics for the rest of the query and uses its normal cardinality estimates instead.
Negative values are rejected with an error.

ul.li: This option takes effect only when USE_HBO_STATS is set to true. Otherwise, the planner does not read HBO statistics and there is nothing to limit.

The limit applies to the total time of all HBO lookups for the query, summed over all plan nodes. This is the value of the HBOStats.TotalTime counter in the Frontend section of the query profile. The time includes both generating the hash keys and reading from the cache backend.

The planner checks the limit before it looks up the statistics for each plan node. The plan node whose lookup crosses the limit still completes its lookup, so the total time can exceed the limit by about the cost of one plan node lookup. Every later plan node skips the HBO lookup and keeps its normal, non-HBO cardinality estimate.
If Impala plans the query more than once, for example when it tries several executor group sets, all of the planning attempts share one time budget.
The option affects only reading HBO statistics. It does not affect STORE_HBO_STATS, and the time spent storing statistics does not count against the limit.

Because the planner skips some HBO lookups, the plan can differ from the plan that it would produce with no limit. Plan nodes that skip the lookup do not show the "from HBO" annotation in the EXPLAIN output or in the query plan in the profile.

p.b: Observability when the limit is reached:

ul.li: The HBOStats.SkippedCount counter in the Frontend section of the query profile shows how many plan node lookups the planner skipped. The counter appears only when at least one lookup was skipped.

The coordinator log contains one warning for the query. The warning has the following format, which is wrapped here for readability: HBO is turned off for the rest of this query since the time limit is reached: HBOStats.TotalTime=..., hbo_max_read_time_ms=...

conbody.p: Run the following command to remove the limit:SET HBO_MAX_READ_TIME_MS=0;
